title: Inexactness of SDP relaxation and valid inequalities for optimal power flow
contribution: Shows that with generation lower bounds the SDP/SOCP relaxation of radial AC-OPF can be exact, inexact or feasible while OPF is infeasible (complete closed-form classification for the two-bus system), releases a library of radial MATPOWER-derived instances with large relaxation gaps, and gives SOCP-based bound tightening and secant cuts that let BARON solve them much faster (read: arXiv:1410.1004v3).
problem_entry: Tests the hypothesis shared by recent SDP-exactness theorems (no generation lower bounds on radial networks), justified by ramping constraints in practice; goal stated as two fold: show inexactness, then make global-solution progress (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: All radial-OPF nonconvexity lies in c_ij^2+s_ij^2=c_ii c_jj; for two buses eliminate to the (c11,c22) plane and classify outcomes geometrically; algorithmically, tighten c/s bounds by SOCP relaxations and cut the bound box away from the inner disc of the ring, feeding BARON the radial reformulation (pp. 6, 8-11, 18-20).
assumptions: Radial networks (reformulation exact only there); SOCP=SDP on radial networks taken from cited [21]; two-bus: g=b=0, G<0, B>0, linear cost; examples: V in [0.9,1.1], large line limits; cuts assume lower bound on c_ij > 0, claimed not restrictive (pp. 3, 5-6, 12, 18).
proof_devices: elimination of the linear power-balance system to express all variables in (c11,c22) (eqs. (7)-(9), p. 8)
hyperbola (10) with asymptotes and generator bounds as a band parallel to the first asymptote (p. 8)
linear objective level sets parallel to the band, so only lower bounds matter; effective lower bound Delta (eq. (11), pp. 8-9)
case analysis by named intersection points c^O, c^R, c^E, c^L, c^I with closed-form gap -G(c^L_22 - c^I_22) (eqs. (12)-(16), Theorem 3.1, pp. 9-11)
repair argument: shift c11, c22, c12 down equally from an SOCP-optimal point to reach the OPF optimum c^E (p. 11)
validity of secant cut: points cut off from the box lie inside the inner circle of radius Vmin_i Vmin_j (Algorithm 1, pp. 18-20)
experiments: Load-scaling sweeps on 2- and 3-bus examples (Tables 2-3, p. 14); radial library from MATPOWER 9-57 bus via spanning trees, SDP (MOSEK) vs BARON (gap 0) vs MATPOWER vs IPOPT with objective, time, rank and dispatch-distance check (Table 4, pp. 15-17); BARON with bounds and cuts reporting preprocessing/total time and root gap, including cases where overhead hurts (Table 5, pp. 20-22); hardware stated (p. 17).
positioning: Sorts OPF work into local, convex-relaxation and global methods (global 'in their infancy'); restates SDP exactness results with their hypotheses, agrees with [26] in the exact case, shows [13] does not extend to reactive lower bounds; sets aside the moment hierarchy as possibly impractical; closes by affirming SDP's importance (pp. 2-3, 9, 12, 22).
writing: Enumerated trichotomy in the abstract; roadmap paragraph; figures carry the geometry; theorem stated after the case analysis ('The above analysis proves the following theorem.'); appendix explaining BARON to power engineers; negative cut results stated plainly (pp. 1, 3, 7-11, 22-23).
limits_future: Reformulation valid only for radial networks, so BARON approach may not scale to large OPF; cuts do not improve SOCP/SDP bounds; preprocessing dominates on small cases; future: efficient global OPF methods, cuts for meshed networks and as LMIs for SDP (claimed, untested) (pp. 17, 20, 22).

method_links.note: published SDP-exactness theorem demarcated by a complete classification of outcomes on the two-bus system plus a counterexample showing another positive result does not extend to reactive lower bounds

relaxation judged against BARON certified global optimum (relative gap 0) and local solvers; dispatch-distance check that gaps are not cost artifacts; also Heuristics 1 (radial instance library released), 2, 3 and 6 (preprocessing overhead counted)

first paper of the OPF arc: the cheap SOCP/SDP relaxation is shown inexact and the certificate comes from BARON strengthened by SOCP-based bound tightening and cuts, which do not improve the SOCP bound itself; the cheap-relaxation-as-deliverable stance appears only in the later Strong SOCP paper
weak: 'all the nonconvexity' isolated in the per-line coupling constraint and cuts derived from the small box-vs-ring set per line, but no hull or substructure theory

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: complete classification on the smallest instance
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: closed-form classification of all SOCP/SDP outcomes (exact, finite gap, OPF infeasible) for the two-bus one-generator system before larger counterexamples
load scaling gamma moves 2-bus and 3-bus examples through exact, gap and infeasible-but-relaxation-feasible regimes, tabulated

transferable: List each published exactness result with its hypothesis, find the hypothesis all of them drop, and justify from practice why it matters (pp. 2-3).
Eliminate linear equalities down to two variables on the smallest instance and classify relaxation outcomes by named intersection points; state the theorem as inequalities among them (pp. 8-11).
Build counterexample instances from standard benchmarks by a structural restriction (spanning tree) plus parameter changes only, keep them realistic and post them (p. 15).
Optimization-based bound tightening with the convex relaxation followed by a secant cut separating the bound box from the infeasible inner disc of an annulus constraint (Algorithm 1, pp. 18-20).
Report preprocessing, solver and total time plus root gap, including instances where the added machinery hurts (Table 5, pp. 20-22).
When an objective gap could be blamed on cost scaling, also report the distance between relaxed and globally optimal decisions (p. 17).

quotes.text: Although, for our instances, we have not observed any lower bound improvement in SOCP/SDP relaxations by the inclusion of the valid inequalities, we obtain stronger root node relaxations in BARON.
Our work only serves to demonstrate the limitations of SDP relaxations and emphasizes the importance and the need to develop efficient global methods in solving OPF problems.
